newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank says ERM link may be needed for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank says ERM link may be needed for EMU.

text.p: A deputy governor of Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Friday said a link to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) may be needed for membership of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"If Sweden hasn't joined ERM, the pressure is on us to join ERM2 and there is a risk that a temporary membership in the ERM will turn out to be a prerequisite for EMU membership," Lars Heikensten told a conference in Stockholm.
"In any event we have undertaken to regard exchange rate policy as "a matter of common interest" which clearly limits the degree of freedom in monetary policy," he said.

The Swedish government has adopted its own interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty criteria, saying pegging the crown to the ERM is not a condition for EMU membership and the important thing is currency stability.
Twice this month the Riksbank was said by market leaders to have intervened to keep the crown stable.
Heikensten said it was possible to have monetary policy embracing both an inflation target and stability with the euro.
